agents.brief: Independent critic of the founder's GBM result (exec-452084f7, /work/pred/run.py, code blob c5064f90...). Check for leakage in the CV, rerun under a GroupKFold-by-position split and compare to the one-hot ridge baseline under the same split, and check per-dataset gains. Publish a null_result or finding for each conclusion with exec evidence. Post key numbers on the board.

Build on the founder's GBM result (exec-452084f7, /work/pred/run.py, code blob c5064f90...). It uses gradient boosting over leave-one-out target encodings (position, sliding window, mutant aa, wt->mt pair, position x mutant class) plus KD/volume features, and beats one-hot ridge on all 8 DMS datasets in 5-fold CV (mean MAE 0.3008 baseline vs 0.2426 model). Improve it: add BLOSUM62 (hardcode the matrix, no internet), per-position statistics (median, min, max, fraction deleterious), and ensembling with ridge. Run every experiment with lab exec on your own copy, compare mean CV MAE to 0.2426, and publish an 'extends' finding with a prediction test that cites exec-452084f7 and uses the founder's code blob via relations. Only claim numbers that appear in your exec metrics.json. Post results on the board.

artifacts.title: Sibling-assay gain comes almost entirely from same-variant sibling scores, not position means
artifacts.summary: Decomposes the cross-assay transfer gain (exec-84e0fa55) on the six sibling-covered datasets using the same 5-fold folds (exec-4f34cf41). For 96-100% of held-out variants the sibling assay contains an exact (pos,mut) match. Same-variant-only sibling features reproduce the full gain: mean MAE 0.1473 vs 0.1470 with both feature sets. Position-mean-only sibling features recover little: 0.1990 vs 0.2058 without siblings. Implication: the sibling transfer is mostly a measured-variant lookup in a correlated assay. It should hold on the hidden split only if hidden variants also appear in the sibling train files, which the CV overlap suggests. This qualifies the six sibling-transfer findings (findin-7d7426c5, -415cf430, -132a1f30, -c2cee133, -d4e5f6c7, -fe58186e); it does not refute them.
